findings.title: forEach with async callback loses error handling and never waits
findings.body: At packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125, the code runs `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` inside a try/catch (lines 124-139). Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the Promise returned by the async arrow is discarded, and the await on getCalendar (line 128) and the returned `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` Promise are fire-and-forget. With getCalendar now async, the dynamic import inside it can reject, and that rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection - the surrounding try/catch cannot see errors thrown after the first await inside the callback. Consequence: when a calendar integration fails to load or delete an event during a reschedule, the error is silently dropped (only Node's unhandledRejection handler sees it), the try/catch's logger.error is never invoked, and the user may see a booking marked as rescheduled while the old event remains on their calendar. Replace forEach by `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => { ... }))` (or a for-of loop with await), and move any try/catch inside the async function so rejections can be caught.

findings.title: forEach with async callback loses error handling and never waits
findings.body: Same bug pattern as the vital reschedule file: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` at line 125 is wrapped in a try/catch (lines 124-139), but forEach does not await the async callback, so rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` (line 128) and from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled promise rejections. The `await getCalendar` added by this PR is a new place where async errors can occur (dynamic import rejection), and the try/catch is now actively misleading because it looks like errors will be logged but they will not be. Use Promise.all + an inner try/catch (or for-of with await) instead of forEach.

findings.title: forEach with async callback never awaits and there is no error handling
findings.body: In the requestReschedule mutation at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` fires off calendar deletions without awaiting. There is no try/catch around it. The mutation proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail and to await the webhook promises, then returns - the deletions may still be in flight or have failed silently. With getCalendar now async, a rejection from the dynamic import (e.g., app module missing or throwing on evaluation) becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Consequence: reschedule can be marked successful in the DB and the user notified, while the old calendar event is never deleted and the error is silently lost. Replace the forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => { ... }))` (or a for-of with await) and add per-iteration error handling so failures are at least logged.

findings.title: forEach with async callback in recurring-event cancellation never awaits and lacks error handling
findings.body: In the recurring-event branch of handleCancelBooking at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential); ... await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); ... })` is fire-and-forget: forEach does not await async callbacks. There is no try/catch around this code. The await on getCalendar (added by this PR, now an async function whose dynamic import can reject) and on deleteEvent produce unawaited promises. Consequence: recurring-event cancellations can leave orphan events on user calendars, and any rejection from a missing/broken app module is an unhandled rejection with no logger entry. Replace with `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async (credential) => { ... }))` and add a try/catch inside the callback to log failures.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters awaits each dynamic import sequentially
findings.body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts:21-36, getVideoAdapters is implemented as `for (const cred of withCredentials) { ... const app = await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore]; ... }`. Previously this was a synchronous reduce over already-bundled modules; the PR conversion to async made every iteration await the dynamic import in series. For a user with multiple video integrations (e.g. zoom + daily + googlemeet) the dynamic imports are done sequentially when they could run concurrently via `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(async (cred) => { ... }))`. While each individual import is typically fast, this is a clear performance regression introduced by the refactor and is worth parallelizing.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials keeps a sync signature but returns objects with unawaited Promises
findings.body: At packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:23-36, getCalendarCredentials is still declared as a synchronous function but now stores the result of `getCalendar(credential)` (which became async and returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`) in each item's `calendar` field (line 28). The caller must remember to `await item.calendar` individually. The diff updates getConnectedCalendars to do this (line 48), but the API contract is unsound: any other caller (existing or future) that uses the returned items expecting `calendar` to be a Calendar (or just checks `if (!calendar)` to short-circuit) will be wrong - a Promise is always truthy. Either make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar inside, or memoize a synchronous module loader so getCalendar can stay sync and the field type is preserved.
